SR Pal, Senior Advocate, AFM Mesbahuddin Advocate, with him, instructed by Shamsul Haque Siddique, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Respondents ----- Not represented.

Atiqullah (Md) ------ Petitioner

full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury, J. : This petition for leave to appeal is from an order dated 7 March 1996 of a Single Judge of the High Court Division summarily rejecting a revisional application preferred by the petitioner under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act for setting aside the decree of the Small Cause Court Judge (Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court), Dhaka for his eviction in SCC Suit No.8 of 1994. It is out of time by 17 days. As the petitioners have explained the delay satisfactorily we condone the delay. 

 3. The trial Court believed the case of the respondents that the petitioner was a tenant under them and that he failed to make payment of any rent from January 1991 and accordingly decreed the suit on 27 January 1990 over-ruling the objection of the petitioner. Petitioner thereafter unsuccessfully moved the High Court Division under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act. 

 4. Mr. SR Pal, learned Counsel on behalf of the petitioner, submits that since the petitioner is a co-sharer in respect of the suit premises by way of purchase the suit for eviction on the ground of default in payment of rents was to fail. The learned Judge of the High Court Division has, therefore, erred in law in refusing to set aside the decree passed by the trial Court. 

 5. It is the consistent view of this court that once it is established that a person is a tenant he cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord as a subsequent purchaser from a co-sharer without surrendering his possession to his landlord. As, in the instant case, it is found that the petitioner was a tenant under the respondents to whom he paid rents upto December, 1990, he is debarred from setting up a claim of title in himself to resist the decree for eviction.
